name: Lombard

ancestors.notes: Celtic (Lepontic/Insubric) substrate: significant in the Po Valley before Roman conquest. Possible influence on vowel system.
Lombardic superstrate (6th–8th c.): the Lombards gave their name to the region. Lexical influence, possible phonological.

notes: Lombard. Gallo-Italic language of Lombardy, parts of Piedmont, and Swiss Ticino. ~3.5 million speakers. Reference variety: Western Lombard (Milanese). Key features: (1) Front rounded vowels /y, ø/. (2) Phonemic vowel length. (3) Degemination. (4) Extreme final vowel loss. (5) Intervocalic lenition (Sanga 1984). Stress exemption: Lombard word stress is lexical/unpredictable from spelling (the orthography does not mark it and vowel reduction patterns vary by sub-dialect); no stress block is declared. Source: Loporcaro, Michele (2009), Profilo linguistico dei dialetti italiani, on Gallo-Italic stress and vowel reduction; Maiden & Parry (1997), The Dialects of Italy. Accented vowels à/è/é/ì/í/ò/ó follow the Ticinese orthography (Salvioni 1907, codified by the Centro di dialettologia e di etnografia del Canton Ticino, the only Lombard orthography with public/official status): grave marks the open timbre (è=/ɛ/, ò=/ɔ/) and acute the closed timbre (é=/e/, ó=/o/) of the stressed vowel, following the Italian-orthography convention the Ticinese system explicitly borrows; à/ì/í mark stress only, since Lombard (like Italian) does not distinguish open/closed timbre on a/i. â/ê/ô follow the classical Milanese orthography (Circolo Filologico Milanese revision of Maggi/Porta-era usage), whose 'Accenti' section states the circumflex marks a 'very closed timbre and long duration' and gives ô and û as its worked examples; â and ê are only covered by a trailing 'ecc.' and are not separately illustrated. That same source also states plain ⟨o⟩ is already 'pronunciata come u italiana' in Milanese, so a circumflex applied to an already-[u] vowel gives [uː] by the source's own logic, not [oː]; ô is mapped to /u/ here rather than /uː/ because the only two circumflex-o words in the WikiPron gold ('rasô', 'resô') both realize as plain /u/ with no length, so the length component of the source's rule is not shipped for ô — this is a measured, not sourced, choice for length specifically, while the /u/-not-/o/ timbre is the source's own stated rule. â is shipped as plain /a/, not /aː/: the source never actually illustrates â (it falls under 'ecc.' only), and the WikiPron gold is a coin flip on length for it ('citâ'/'çitâ', 2 words, show /aː/; 'jâld'/'tajâ', 2 words, show no length across all 6 attested lines), so no length claim is asserted for â. ê is kept as /eː/ (matching the source's stated circumflex-length rule) but rests on a single gold attestation ('paês' → /p a eː s/, n=1), which is too thin to confirm or refute the rule on its own; treat this mapping as source-derived, not gold-confirmed. û is left unmapped: the source names it as one of its two worked circumflex examples, but û never occurs in the WikiPron gold, so there is no distributional check available and no mapping is shipped rather than guessing. œ is treated as the Unicode-ligature form of the classical digraph 'oeu' (=ö=/ø/ in the Ticinese/classical comparison table). x, y and ç remain unmapped: no primary source describes a stable phonemic value for them in Lombard orthography (neither the Ticinese nor the classical Milanese vowel/consonant tables list x or y at all), and the one experimental orthography that defines ç (as /z/ or /tʃ/, per it.wikipedia 'Lingua lombarda' 'Ortografie sperimentali') both never caught on and does not match the realizations attested for ç in the WikiPron gold, which skew towards /s/, /ʃ/ and /ts/ instead. Sources: it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortografia_ticinese (accent table, 'Vocali'/'Accentazione'/'Vocali lunghe' sections, citing Salvioni 1907 and CDE Canton Ticino); it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortografia_milanese_classica ('Principi generali'/'Accenti', citing Porta, Poesie, ed. Isella, Mondadori 1982); it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_lombarda ('Sistema di scrittura' section, for the experimental-orthography ç value and the classical no-diacritics baseline).
